posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

The field of astronomy grew rapidly as new instruments were crafted to make discoveries, as you can see on the August page of our 12,026 Human Era calendar. That is when champions like Tycho Brahe, an eccentric man with a metal nose, achieved notoriety by throwing astronomy parties and collecting great volumes of star data that we still use today.

Euro summer at the tourist hotspots is an adventure of its own. ⁠
Just remember to show up when you hear your name! 😂⁠
⁠
🎥: @aditijhaveri_

Gullholmen is a small island off Sweden’s west coast, where wooden houses are located right next to each other.⁠
⁠
The island grew as a fishing community, and with so little space available, homes were built close together, creating the narrow lanes and passages that still give Gullholmen its character today.⁠
⁠
Would you visit this little fishing village?⁠
⁠
By: @mannsheimerphoto

Expectation vs reality with a condor. 😂🦅⁠
Getting the perfect photo with one of the world's largest flying birds isn't always as easy as it looks.⁠
⁠
Would you pay for a photo with a condor? 😅⁠
🎥: @bobbi.sfredda

What a climb! ⛰️⁠
noah.vie and the crew took on the steep steps leading to China's famous Avatar Mountains, where every step is rewarded with breathtaking views.⁠
⁠
Located in Zhangjiajie National Forest Park, these towering sandstone pillars are said to have inspired the floating mountains seen in Avatar.⁠
Would you make the climb for views like these?

Every summer, Hala Gąsienicowa in Poland’s Tatra Mountains turns pink as fireweed covers parts of the mountain meadow. 🌸⁠
⁠
The flowers usually bloom from late July to around mid-August, and the display only lasts for about two to three weeks.⁠
⁠
With the Tatra peaks rising behind the flowers, it’s one of the most beautiful signs that summer is coming to an end in the mountains.⁠
⁠
By: @borievkyphotogallery @karolnienartowicz

A side of Indonesia where life moves at a different pace. 🌿✨⁠
⁠
Sulawesi is a destination of lush landscapes, peaceful villages, and breathtaking nature, making it the perfect place to slow down, take a breath, and enjoy the moment.⁠
⁠
🎥: @avafgrace

A rare white orca was spotted off the coast of Rausu in Hokkaido, Japan.⁠
⁠
The sighting was captured by nature photographer Tokuyuki Hayakawa, who has spent 15 years photographing orcas in the area.⁠
⁠
The whale is believed to be male and around 8 meters long.⁠
⁠
Locals sometimes refer to these rare white orcas as “phantoms.” 🐋⁠
⁠
By: @shiretoko_orca_photo_album

A whole experience awaits at this restaurant in Japan. 🎣⁠
A dining spot where guests can catch their own fish before enjoying it freshly prepared for their meal.⁠
⁠
A fun and interactive way to experience Japanese cuisine that turns dinner into an adventure.⁠
⁠
Who would love to try this? 🐟🍣⁠
🎥: @_queen.sav_

@yourworldmylens turns the Moon into the star of his photographs, using perspective, timing, and a little imagination to create playful scenes that make you look twice. ⁠
⁠
His photos play with scale and perspective, turning the Moon into everything from part of a pair of headphones to something you could almost reach out and pick up. ⁠
⁠
Each image uses timing and composition to create a little visual illusion around our closest celestial neighbor. 🌕⁠
⁠
Which photo is your favorite?

Some travel moments simply can't be planned. ✨👑⁠
⁠
While exploring the Himalayasan unexpected encounter turned into a story for a lifetime, meeting the Queen Mother of Bhutan and hearing firsthand about one of the world's most fascinating royal families.⁠
⁠
A reminder that travel isn't just about places, but about the people, stories, and surprises you find along the way. 🌏💫⁠
⁠
🎥: @genomada_

There’s a football stadium in Norway where the ocean is practically part of the view from every angle. ⚽️⁠
⁠
Henningsvær Stadion sits on a rocky islet in the Lofoten Islands, surrounded by the sea, jagged rocks, and dramatic mountains. It’s a local amateur pitch with no grandstands, but its unusual setting has made it famous far beyond this tiny fishing village⁠.⁠
⁠

Spotted lanternflies, accidentally introduced to the U.S. in 2014, are munching their way through the Northeast and Midwest. These invasive insects pose a serious threat to farmers' crops and the wine industry, potentially costing some state economies over half a billion dollars. While some people are still squashing them on sight, others are turning to a more unexpected ally to help stop the spread.

Head to the link in bio to learn more about the environmental impact of spotted lanternflies an

Native Hawaiian snails are in trouble, but efforts are underway to protect these colorful creatures from the invasive species that threaten them. 🐌 Are you a snail aficionado like @joelsartore?

We’re celebrating 20 years of the National Geographic #PhotoArk, an audacious project documenting the world's incredible biodiversity and highlighting the importance of conservation through photography. Which animal do you want to see next?

Astronomers have found a Jupiter-sized world orbiting a brown dwarf 73 light-years away—and they can't agree on what to call it. Moon? Planet? They've settled, for now, on "exosatellite." Twenty years after the International Astronomical Union voted to define "planet" and demoted Pluto in the process, the line is still blurry.

See what counts as a planet—and what doesn't—at the link in bio.

As the school year starts up again, pencils are sharpened, lunches are packed—and cases of head lice are on the rise.

Affecting up to 12 million American children between the ages of 3 and 11 every year, these blood-sucking parasites cause discomfort, infection, and, in more extreme cases, bug-related paranoia.

Though they’ve itched us for millennia, the nature of how they spread and how best to eradicate them is still a bit of a head-scratcher.

A flamboyance of flamingos fly over Lake Logipi in northern Kenya, a refuge and active breeding ground for the country's millions of flamingos. Photographer Alexander Ley (@wildlife_ley)captured their flight from the opening of a doorless helicopter, using the lake's shallow water, algae, and mineral-rich shoreline as the backdrop.

See more Photos of the Day at the link in bio.

For juvenile Kemp’s ridley sea turtles like Lucky, warming oceans can carry them farther north than expected. But when temperatures drop in these northern waters, the cold can leave them unable to swim, increasing the risk of strandings far from their tropical habitat.

Learn more about Lucky and other cold-stunned turtles at the link in bio. 

Video by Atlantis Paradise Island, Bahamas

Photograph by @mitchell.leong | Bathed in the soft glow of the rising sun, a mountain goat stands tall amid a vibrant meadow of wildflowers in the Canadian Rockies. The stillness was broken only by the rustling flowers, buzzing bees, and occasional whispering wind. It was an unparalleled moment in a vast wilderness that felt both eternal and fragile.

This photo was featured in our #NatGeoYourShotOurHOME challenge.

Retiring at 100 years old? Not a chance! Here’s a sneak peek of Sir David Attenborough working on the narration for the upcoming BLUE PLANET III.

#DavidAttenborough100 #DavidAttenborough #BluePlanetIII

Finding your feet 👣

Over 500 million years ago, flecks of food drifting on ocean currents were eaten by small animals on the seabed, but the flow would often change. To reach them, some tried a pioneering action: they would move. These are thought to be some of the first animal tracks on Earth.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Who knew the ocean has a public transport system 🦀
 
Columbus crabs aren’t built for long-distance swimming, so this little crab takes a shortcut through the open ocean. By hitchhiking a ride on a turtle, he find transport, a new home and some unexpected company.
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

More than meets the eye 👀

Ancient ancestors of the dolphin hid from the sun’s UV rays using two light-detecting spots. Fascinatingly, some inherited mutations that allowed them to perceive light and shade together, so they could visualise their environment - essentially becoming the first proper eyes.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

From fantasy to reality 🦇

Evolution presenter @chrisgpackham2 reveals how coming face-to-face with some extraordinary bats fulfilled a childhood dream.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Turns out the forest has a group chat 📞
 
Treehoppers might be tiny, but they’ve got plenty to say! They communicate through vibrations sent along the plants they live on, most of which are too quiet for us to hear. But when danger appears, sending the right signal can make all the difference. 
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

Becoming 'Ant Enemy Number One' 🐜

Army ants are very protective of their colonies, as @chrisgpackham2 found out. Chris reveals how he tackled the challenge of presenting to camera whilst being bitten in some surprisingly painful places! 

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Man’s best friend 🐶

Dogs move differently to humans. They have a digitigrade posture, which means they walk on their toe bones. This anatomy allows longer and more efficient strides so they run faster and jump further. With less surface area touching the ground, they also move with more agility and greater stealth.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

That’s one lucky impala 
 
Leopards rely on stealth and lightening speed to bring down prey, but a successful hunt can quickly attract unwanted attention. When a spotted hyena arrives to challenge the leopard’s hard-earned catch, an unexpected chain of events unfolds.

This unique stealing and bartering behaviour has been observed among Uluwatu’s macaques for more than 30 years. Younger monkeys learn it from older members of the group, allowing the tradition to be passed down through generations.
